blogs.title: The 'Legislature Knows How' Canon: Parsing Private Enforcement Rights Under Minnesota Wage Law
blogs.description: This post will analyze the Eighth Circuit's use of statutory interpretation principles to hold that the Minnesota Payment of Wages Act does not authorize private employees to seek average daily wage penalties—a power reserved exclusively to the state Commissioner. The analysis will examine the court's reasoning comparing § 181.101 with other Minnesota statutes that explicitly grant penalty authority to employees, and discuss the broader implications for how courts determine legislative intent regarding enforcement mechanisms in state labor laws.

blogs.title: Mootness and Civil Penalties: When Does Full Compensation End a Plaintiff's Stake in the Case?
blogs.description: This post will examine the Eighth Circuit's concerns about whether Cohen retained standing to seek statutory penalties after stipulating that he had received all owed wages and liquidated damages. The discussion will analyze the application of Supreme Court precedent from Friends of the Earth v. Laidlaw to wage and hour litigation, the potential for defendants to strategically moot claims through payment, and the unresolved tension between deterrence goals and Article III standing requirements.

blogs.title: Procedural Lessons from Cohen v. Consilio: Preserving Claims and Proper Pleading in Wage Litigation
blogs.description: This post will discuss the procedural missteps that doomed portions of Cohen's appeal, including the waiver of the MWTA claim for lack of meaningful argument and the rejection of the injunctive relief claim for improper presentation during summary judgment. The analysis will cover practical lessons for litigating wage and hour cases, the importance of properly amending pleadings rather than raising new claims in briefing, and strategies for preserving issues for appellate review.
